edges.name: Market intraday momentum (last 30 minutes)
edges.mechanism: Structural: short-gamma hedging by option dealers and leveraged-ETF rebalancing near the close; infrequent rebalancing; late-informed trading

sources.citation: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018). Market intraday momentum. Journal of Financial Economics 129(2):394-414
key_facts: r1 = prior close -> 10:00 ET predicts r13 = 15:30-16:00; R2 1.6% (2.6% with r12); OOS R2 1.4% / 2.0%
sign(r1) timing 6.67%/yr, sd 6.19%, Sharpe 1.08 vs buy-and-hold 0.29
after spreads (Jul 2001-2013) 4.46%/yr; post-2005 6.52% net vs 7.96% gross; SPY spread ~1.2 bps after 2005
stronger on high-vol, high-volume, recession and macro-news days

sources.citation: Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (2021). Hedging demand and market intraday momentum. Journal of Financial Economics 142(1):377-403
key_facts: r_ROD (prior close -> close-30m) predicts r_LH (last 30m) in all asset classes
timing Sharpe 0.87-1.73 per asset class, transaction costs NOT considered
stronger when dealers are more short gamma; last-30m move reverses over next 3 days

sources.citation: Li, Sakkas & Urquhart (2022). Journal of Financial Markets 57:100619
key_facts: significant in- and out-of-sample in most markets; stronger with low liquidity, high volatility, discrete information

contrary.citation: Rosa (2022). Understanding intraday momentum strategies. Journal of Futures Markets 42(12):2218-2234
key_facts: predictability disappears out of sample
depends on signal strength; thresholded strategy beats always-on

contrary.citation: Dim, Eraker & Vilkov (2024). 0DTEs: Trading, Gamma Risk and Volatility Propagation. SSRN 4692190
key_facts: positive (negative) dealer gamma strengthens intraday reversal (momentum)

spec.rosa_threshold: trade only if |signal| > k*rolling_sd(N); k,N pre-registered

sqx_requirements: custom block: session-anchored return (prior cash close -> T-30)
limit time range + exit at end of range

edges.name: Index short-term mean reversion (IBS / N-day low)
edges.mechanism: Index-product arbitrage makes index returns negatively autocorrelated; liquidity provision pays more in high VIX

key_facts: thresholds ~0.4/~0.9; stronger in high vol, Mondays; disappears on low-volume days (US)
little or no effect in local ETFs of FR, AU, DE, ES, CH, TW, UK

USD up European open->London fix 1.7 bps/day (t=4.1); down after London fix 1.9 bps/day (t=5.5)

key_facts: domestic currencies depreciate in domestic hours
